subject: Chemistry
title: Streptomycin: Defeating Tuberculosis
description: A 60-second lesson on Streptomycin: Defeating Tuberculosis.

hook.text: Tuberculosis killed 1 in 4 Europeans in the 1800s. In 1943, streptomycin became the first drug to defeat it.

buildup.text: Albert Schatz found streptomycin in soil bacteria (Streptomyces griseus). Soil teems with organisms producing natural antibiotics.

discovery.text: Streptomycin blocks bacterial ribosomes from making proteins. Without proteins, TB bacteria can't grow or reproduce.

twist.text: Schatz's supervisor, Selman Waksman, took sole credit and the Nobel Prize. Schatz sued and won partial recognition.

climax.text: TB still kills 1.3 million people yearly. Drug-resistant TB strains now require 6-month cocktails of multiple antibiotics.

punchline.text: A soil bacterium's weapon against competitors became humanity's cure for TB.

quiz.question: Where was streptomycin discovered?
options: In soil bacteria that produce natural antibiotics to compete with other microbes
In deep-sea sponges collected from the Pacific Ocean
In the blood of people who had recovered from tuberculosis

details.summary: Streptomycin, isolated by Albert Schatz and Selman Waksman in 1943 from soil bacteria Streptomyces griseus, was the first effective treatment for tuberculosis. It binds to the 30S ribosomal subunit and causes misreading of the genetic code, producing faulty proteins that kill the bacteria.
details.whyItMatters: Streptomycin proved that antibiotics from soil bacteria could treat diseases resistant to penicillin. It launched systematic screening of soil microorganisms that produced dozens of antibiotics still used today.
takeaways: Streptomycin binds bacterial ribosomes, causing lethal protein errors
It was the first drug to effectively treat tuberculosis in 1944
Soil bacteria screening inspired by this discovery yielded many antibiotics

faq.question: How does streptomycin kill tuberculosis bacteria specifically?
faq.answer: Streptomycin binds irreversibly to the 16S rRNA of the 30S ribosomal subunit, distorting the decoding site. This causes the ribosome to misread mRNA codons, inserting wrong amino acids into proteins. The accumulation of misfolded, non-functional proteins is lethal to the bacteria.

faq.question: Why must tuberculosis be treated with multiple drugs simultaneously?
faq.answer: TB bacteria mutate frequently, and monotherapy quickly selects for resistant strains. Multi-drug regimens target different bacterial processes simultaneously, making it statistically near-impossible for a single bacterium to develop resistance to all drugs at once..
